chunks: Say to the desert Arabs who had stayed behind: 'You will be called against a formidable people. You will fight them till they surrender. If you obey, then He will give you a good reward; but if you turn back, as you had done before, He will punish you with a grievous affliction.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the verse addressing the desert Arabs who stayed behind?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the expedition to Tabuk, highlighting the transition from the internal consolidation of the Muslim community to external military engagement against the Byzantines. It underscores the principle of *Tawalli* and *Tabarri* by contrasting the reward for those who follow the Imam with the punishment for those who revert to their pre-Islamic stubbornness, serving as a paradigm for communal obedience.
